claim: Talon.One's core product is an omnichannel promotion and loyalty engine for enterprises, with modules for Enterprise Loyalty Management, Offer Management & Execution, Personalized Promotions, and Talon.One Predict (ML/AI promotion optimization).
page_title: Talon.One — The world's most powerful incentives engine
notes: Homepage module structure; named customers include Adidas, Sephora, Panera, Ticketmaster, Lush.

claim: Talon.One serves 40+ named enterprise customers including Adidas, Sephora, Nordstrom, ASOS, KFC, Ticketmaster, Estee Lauder, Gymshark, EE/BT, with case metrics such as Panera's 60-million-member loyalty program, Bilt Rewards 5M+ members, MoneySuperMarket 2M+ member club.
notes: Scale evidence for enterprise production decisioning.

claim: Adyen announced acquisition of Talon.One on 2026-04-23 for EUR 750M and completed it on 2026-07-01; Adyen plans to combine 'Adyen's global payments infrastructure and proprietary transaction data with Talon.One's real-time decisioning capabilities' to adjust promotions/pricing based on consumer identity.
page_title: Adyen completes acquisitions of Talon.One and Orb
notes: Corroborated by adyen.com press release, talon.one blog, fintech.global (EUR 750m figure), PYMNTS, Banking Dive. Adyen is now the parent company; strategically material.

claim: Rules consist of conditions that, when met, trigger effects; the Rule Builder exposes built-in and custom attributes via an Attribute Selector (plus filter and placeholder attributes); conditions can be combined with All/At-least-one logic and are evaluated in order of appearance.
notes: Also from docs/product/rules/conditions/using-conditions. Promotion rules and strikethrough rules are the two rule types.

claim: The rule engine runs Talang, a custom Lisp-dialect language implemented in Go and open-sourced by Talon.One; rules are made of Conditions (predicates evaluating to boolean) and Effects (expressions returning side effects).
page_title: talon-one/talang - A custom programming language (lisp-dialect) used at Talon.One
notes: Playground at talang-land.talon.one. Shows the engine is a generic expression evaluator under the promotion domain.

claim: The Integration API's Update customer session endpoint synchronously evaluates the rule engine and always returns an array of effects; each effect carries campaignId, rulesetId, ruleIndex, ruleName, effectType and props.
notes: Effect metadata links every decision output to the campaign, ruleset version ID and rule that produced it.

claim: Documented effect catalog includes acceptCoupon/rejectCoupon, acceptReferral/rejectReferral, setDiscount(+PerItem/PerAdditionalCost), addFreeItem, awardGiveaway/willAwardGiveaway, addLoyaltyPoints/deductLoyaltyPoints, changeLoyaltyTierLevel, updateAttribute, addToAudience, triggerWebhook, showNotification, customEffect, rollback* effects, and error.
notes: Accept/reject exists for codes (binary allow/deny per action); no 'review/hold' output state. customEffect allows developer-defined payloads.

claim: Rejections return machine-readable reason codes, e.g. CouponNotFound, CouponExpired, CouponLimitReached, CouponPartOfNotRunningCampaign, CouponRecipientDoesNotMatch, CouponRejectedByCondition, ProfileLimitReached, CampaignLimitReached, EffectCouldNotBeApplied (budget exhausted); referrals similarly (ReferralCustomerAlreadyReferred, AdvocateNotFound, etc.).
notes: Reason codes are scoped to coupon/referral validation, not to arbitrary decision outcomes.

claim: Integration model: create/update customer profiles (attributes like name, address, history), then update customer sessions (cart items, coupon codes, custom attributes such as shipping city); sessions have states open -> closed / cancelled / partially_returned with documented transitions and rollback effects reverting budgets and redemptions.
notes: Also docs/dev/concepts/entities/customer-sessions. Data model is commerce-session-shaped (cart, order, checkout).

claim: Dry requests: adding dry=true to supported Integration API endpoints evaluates rules without persisting anything; the now query parameter simulates evaluation at a past or future timestamp for time-dependent campaigns; idempotency is not supported for dry requests.
notes: Simulation is per-request what-if, evaluated against CURRENT rules; there is no bulk simulation against historical traffic or historical rule versions.

claim: Audit logs display all changes made via the Management API (columns: User, Application, Entity, Time, Type of change, with JSON detail per entry); access restricted to admins and Application admins; docs suggest using them to revert campaign changes; programmatic access via GET /v1/changes.
notes: Covers configuration changes (who changed what when), not decision traffic. /v1/changes endpoint per Management API SDK docs (getChanges).

claim: Integration API logs record request ID, path, method, response code and time per request; the troubleshooting workflow documents searching these logs by session ID to inspect full request/response pairs; access restricted to admins; retention is governed by contract ('stated in your contract and can be modified').
notes: Full request/response pair inspection confirmed in docs/product/campaigns/troubleshooting-campaigns; retention from docs/product/server-infrastructure-and-data-retention.

claim: Campaign revisions: Running/Scheduled/Expired campaigns can be revised as a copy (states Staged/Revised/Pending); revisions are tested with a testing API key that automatically issues dry requests; finalization applies changes immediately or on a schedule; users without finalization permission can click 'Request Finalization' to notify an admin by email; changes to coupons, referrals, stores, achievements bypass revisions; no revision history view is documented.
notes: This is a staged-change + approval-request pipeline for promotion rules; approver is an admin, with no role semantics for legal/counsel.

claim: Campaign evaluation is deterministic and configurable: campaigns are evaluated one by one per an evaluation tree; evaluation groups define order, scope and mode (First Campaign, Highest Discount, Stackable); within a campaign, cart item filters, rules, conditions and effects evaluate in order of appearance; if an effect cannot be applied the rest of that rule's effects are blocked; budget-exhausted campaigns are skipped.
notes: Also docs/product/applications/managing-campaign-evaluation and setting-up-campaign-priorities.

claim: Campaign budgets restrict total monetary spend, coupon/referral creation and redemptions per campaign or per profile; when multiple budgets target the same effect the most restrictive limit is enforced; discount effects can be allowed to issue partial discounts when remaining budget is insufficient (desiredValue vs actual).
notes: Positioned in docs as security measure against overspending and fraud.

claim: Loyalty engine supports profile-based and card-based programs with subledgers (individual points wallets restricting where points are earned/redeemed); balances are tracked as active, pending, expired and spent; oldest active points are redeemed first (FIFO); points can carry activation and expiry dates set by rule effects.
notes: Also profile-based loyalty docs and addLoyaltyPoints/extendLoyaltyPointsExpiryDate/setLoyaltyPointsExpiryDate effects.

claim: Giveaways: pools store codes/vouchers generated outside Talon.One (e.g., Amazon gift card codes); codes can be imported/exported as CSV; the awardGiveaway effect distributes a code from a pool to a customer when rules match.
notes: Deterministic code distribution to qualifying customers; no sweepstakes/lottery mechanics (no entries, odds, drawings, winner certification).

claim: RBAC: users can be admins or hold roles built from templates (e.g., 'Application Admin' = full Application access); campaign access groups restrict user access to specific campaigns with permission levels View, Create and edit campaigns, Create and edit coupons, and Draft campaigns (create/edit disabled campaigns only).
notes: Also manage-campaign-groups doc; adding an admin to a campaign access group revokes their admin permissions.

claim: SAML single sign-on is supported with Okta and Microsoft Entra ID, including SCIM-based provisioning/deprovisioning and assigning/removing Talon.One roles from the IdP.
notes: Role assignment via Entra ID documented in a dedicated tutorial.

claim: Talon.One states it is 'ISO 27001:2022 certified, GDPR compliant, and holds a SOC 2 Type II attestation'.
notes: Same claims on talon.one product pages and ISO-certification blog post; CCPA compliance claimed on security marketing page.

claim: Infrastructure runs on Google Cloud across multiple availability zones with triple-redundant, self-healing deployments; each customer instance is stored in its own VPC; databases are active-active with warm standby and point-in-time recovery within the last seven days; data retention time is stated in the customer contract and can be modified.
page_title: Data retention policy and server infrastructure | Talon.One docs
notes: Retention is contract-negotiated, not a self-service product control; relevant to D08 scoring.

claim: Developer page claims '50 ms response times up to 2500 rps', '99.9999% 24 month uptime across all customers', and '100M+ campaign evaluations per day'; integration partners include mParticle, Braze, Shopify, Segment, Bloomreach, Commercetools, Salesforce, Iterable, Contentful.
page_title: Developers: SDKs, Documentation and More | Talon.One
notes: Marketing numbers, not an SLA document; production scale corroborated by enterprise customer roster (TALONONE-002).

claim: The Management API ('the API for management purposes and back-office operations') programmatically covers most Campaign Manager functionality (campaigns, custom attributes, loyalty data, audit log /v1/changes) but each endpoint is limited to three requests per second and is explicitly 'not for real-time integrations'; a 2026 endpoint adds automated CSV downloads of raw campaign analytics.
notes: Two-API split: high-throughput Integration API for decisioning; low-rate Management API for configuration.

claim: As of March 11, 2026, the Integration API supports an Idempotency-Key header on the Return cart items endpoint 'as a first step toward supporting idempotent requests across the API'.
notes: Idempotency is new and partial (one endpoint); webhooks carry an X-UUID header for idempotent consumer-side processing.

claim: Outbound webhooks/notifications are configurable (HTTP method, URL, authentication credentials, custom headers); requests fire in real time after qualifying events or on a schedule; all webhooks/notifications carry an X-UUID unique ID header for idempotent processing and have a 10-second response timeout.
notes: Assembled from docs search snippets (outbound-notifications, managing-webhooks, notification schemas); rules can also fire webhooks via the triggerWebhook effect (TALONONE-007).

claim: Platform-wide separation of sandbox and live environments: customer profiles, loyalty programs, audiences and giveaway pools belong to one environment; the environment is determined automatically by the Integration API key used; sandbox data cannot be accessed from live Applications and vice versa.
page_title: Separation of sandbox and live environments | Talon.One docs
notes: Also Applications overview: sandbox vs live Application types.

claim: Applications are the container for campaigns and API keys; accounts typically segment Applications by country, time zone, currency or team; 'You cannot share customer activity or campaigns across different Applications'.
notes: Multi-brand/multi-market by siloed Applications; per-Application API keys; campaign duplication (and 2026 experiment duplication) mitigates but does not remove the silo.

claim: Campaign templates are created from existing campaigns to 'simplify the campaign creation process and increase error control by including predefined rules and restricting the values that can be modified'; placeholders can be range-limited (e.g., discount_percentage 0-20%) or bound to picklists; templates can be used to create campaigns in any Application; states are Draft/Enabled/Disabled.
notes: A governance/guardrail primitive: central teams can lock rule structure and cap parameter ranges for downstream campaign creators. Content is customer-authored promotion logic, not legal policy.

claim: Ledger/data exports exist via UI and Management API: export customer loyalty balances (active, pending, expired, spent), export loyalty card ledger log, export customer transaction logs, and CSV export of customer sessions.
page_title: Managing data for profile-based loyalty programs | Talon.One docs
notes: Endpoint names (exportLoyaltyBalances, exportLoyaltyCardLedger) corroborated by official Postman collection; business-data exports, not a regulator evidence package.

claim: Pricing has three tiers (Starter 'high-growth companies', Professional 'advanced deployments', Enterprise 'large enterprises'); no dollar amounts are published; pricing is 'based on your use of data volume'; all tiers route to contact-sales; Starter includes staging environment, audit logs, user roles; Professional adds dedicated CSM and dedicated database server; Enterprise adds customized SLAs, unlimited users/webhooks, instant troubleshooting.
page_title: Pricing: Find Your Individual Solution | Talon.One
notes: Sales-led motion; no self-serve purchase.

claim: Third-party procurement data (Vendr) reports median Talon.One contract value around $49,011/year with a range of roughly $18,500-$106,350; other third parties estimate entry pricing around EUR 1,500/month.
notes: Third-party estimates; no official confirmation.

claim: Review aggregators (G2/Capterra, 4.7-4.9 ratings) consistently praise Rule Builder flexibility ('virtually any promotional scenario without custom development') and consistently report a steep learning curve, need for significant developer resources for initial integration, and opaque behavior around conflicting campaign rules/stacking.
notes: Market-perception evidence only; one third-party roundup claims 12+ month implementations for legacy-system enterprises.

claim: Promotion-abuse prevention is rule/limit-based: budgets keyed on device IDs, per-profile redemption limits, unique single-use code generation at scale, coupons bound to specific customer IDs, real-time alerts; marketing distinguishes soft fraud (multi-accounting, reward transfer) from hard fraud (bots, coupon farming).
page_title: 7 essential tactics to prevent coupon fraud | Talon.One
notes: No ML fraud scoring, device fingerprinting, or identity-verification product documented; controls are deterministic limits the customer configures.

claim: The financial-services industry documentation covers cashback, gamification/achievements, referral programs and gift cards only; it contains no KYC, AML, jurisdiction-restriction, or regulatory-compliance functionality despite targeting fintech/banking/insurance.
notes: Positive evidence that even for regulated-industry customers, regulatory logic is out of product scope (only the SOC2/ISO/GDPR vendor-posture statement appears).

claim: Talon.One publishes head-to-head comparison pages against Antavo and Eagle Eye; third-party roundups position Talon.One/Voucherify on flexible promotions, Antavo on pure loyalty (no-code, 'AI Loyalty Cloud', 100k+ req/min promotion engine launched May 2025), Eagle Eye on real-time at-POS loyalty/promotions at grocery scale; other adjacent vendors: SAP Emarsys, Punchh, Comarch, LoyaltyLion, Capillary, Uniqodo.
notes: Also talon.one/lp/talon-one-vs-antavo, uniqodo.com and wiserreview.com alternative roundups; competitor claims about Antavo/Eagle Eye are third-party/vendor marketing.

claim: Documented troubleshooting workflow reconstructs past behavior manually: locate the session in the Sessions view, display triggered effects per event in the Events view, search Integration API logs by session ID for full request/response pairs, and cross-reference audit logs to identify rule changes that caused discrepancies; no tool replays historical evaluations or shows intermediate rule-processing state.
notes: Decision reconstruction is possible but manual, ops-oriented, and bounded by contractual log retention; not an evidence/compliance feature.

claim: Concurrency limits are documented: maximum three parallel requests per customer profile/session with a queue of two; excess requests receive HTTP 409; sequential requests are recommended for data integrity.
notes: Integration API global rate limits are not publicly documented (contractual); Management API 3 rps and Segment destination 60 rps are documented.

claim: Official SDKs exist in at least PHP, Java, C#, JavaScript, Python, Ruby and Go (legacy plus 'next-gen' versions), covering both Integration and Management APIs; the current customer session endpoint is v2 (updateCustomerSessionV2) while Management API paths are /v1, showing path-based API versioning.
notes: Official Postman collections also published (Integration API, Management API).

claim: Management API exposes GET /v1/applications/{applicationId}/campaigns/{campaignId}/rulesets (list campaign rulesets) and GET .../rulesets/{rulesetId}; combined with the rulesetId embedded in every returned effect, a customer can programmatically map any logged decision back to the exact ruleset content that produced it.
page_title: Talon.One PHP SDK - Management API endpoints (getRuleset/getRulesets)
notes: Endpoint existence is documented; that rulesets behave as retained immutable versions of rule state is INFERENCE from the ID-per-effect design and list endpoint, not an explicit doc statement.

claim: Campaigns have schedules (start time, end time, or both) interpreted in the Application's time zone; schedules can be modified at any point; revisions can be scheduled to apply at a future time.
notes: Temporal control exists for promotions (activation windows), not for legal effective-date semantics.

claim: The Integration API customer inventory endpoint returns, for one customer, profile information, referral codes, loyalty points/cards and reserved coupons (giveaways loaded per pool), enabling per-customer entitlement lookups.
page_title: Customer session entity / customer inventory | Talon.One docs
notes: Corroborated by SDK getCustomerInventory documentation; used to display wallet contents and check redemption eligibility.

claim: 2026 releases include an Experiments module (A/B experiments can be duplicated across Applications and promoted to regular campaigns), a Management API endpoint for automated CSV downloads of raw campaign analytics, and a price history endpoint for historical SKU data.
notes: Experimentation measures live promo performance; it is not pre-rollout impact analysis against historical traffic.
